title: Logarithmically balanced observations suppress arithmetic phase bias
problem: Remove the scale phase from the R13 Gaussian-weighted limiting observable without changing the underlying walk.
failure: Smoothing alone left a nonconstant phase profile in R13. Uniform sampling in ordinary time is not the same as uniform logarithmic phase averaging; zero displayed spread in a finite sample does not prove exact cancellation.
correction: Average normalized observables over a complete logarithmic period, or use m equally spaced phase shifts that cancel Fourier modes not divisible by m. For this model the limiting bias is at most 1250/(14^m-1). Keep finite-time errors and numerical truncation distinct.
transfer: For an established periodic nuisance parameter, design sampling in its actual phase coordinate, derive a uniform residual bound, and compare against numerical controls. Preserve phase-sensitive data separately when the phase carries information.
limits: R14 concerns a mathematical mixture across observation times with critical Gaussian radius and exact-return normalization. Continuous averaging eliminates limiting phase; finite m has a bound, not exact cancellation. Standard quadrature theory credited. Numerical mean and Bessel orbit evaluations are bounded proxies. No finite-time error rate, actual instrument, independent review, or originality claim.
